title: Maximum residue levels for cycloxydim
summary: EU to increase MRL for cycloxydim in honey from early 2027
update: The European Union (EU) will increase the maximum residue level (MRL) for cycloxydim in honey from 0.05 to 0.6 mg/kg. This follows a positive evaluation of its safety for consumers by the European Food Safety Authority.
what_changing: The EU will increase the MRL for cycloxydim in honey from 0.05 (the limit of determination, LOD) to 0.6 mg/kg. (The LOD is the lowest level that can be detected using the most modern and reliable analytical methods.)
why: Following an application for a change of MRL by the producer of cycloxydim, the European Food Safety Authority concluded that increasing the MRL would not pose a risk for consumers ( EFSA 2026 ).
timeline:
The new MRL in honey is expected to apply from early 2027 .

The MRLs in Table 1 apply from 17 April 2025.
background:
In April 2025, the EU increased the MRLs for cycloxydim on pome fruits, peas, maize, and sugar beet roots as shown in Table 1, following a positive evaluation of their safety for consumers ( EFSA 2024 ).

MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database .
